name: Celebrating James Muriungi Kaburia, from clerk to manager

content.title: Celebrating James Muriungi Kaburia, from clerk to manager
content.summary: James started off as a clerk, and rose up the ladder to become the Medical Record Manager at the Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi.

media.caption: James was celebrated for his 30 years of service at the annual Long Service Awards & Recognitions Ceremony on Wednesday.
media.alt: Celebrating James Muriungi Kaburia, from clerk to manager

content.text: Thirty years ago, a hopeful James Muriungi Kaburia walked through the gates of the Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi (AKUHN). Fresh from college, the 22-year old James was hired to support hospital operations as a clerk to manage patient records among other clerical duties.

Three decades later, two children and a Bachelors of Arts in Leadership and Management degree in his bag - James looks back at his career's journey with pride. He has risen up the ladder from a clerk to the Medical Record Manager and advisor to Record Management at Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi.
We caught up with James, who was celebrated for his 30 years of service at the annual
Long Service Awards & Recognitions Ceremony
on Wednesday.
Let us go back into time - what advice would you give your younger self if today was your first working day at AKUHN?
Be transparent, have a listening ear and passion for hard work. You have both informed peers and experienced leaders, so be ready and willing to learn from them.
What has kept you going over the years?
The desire to produce the best results in business in the most effective manner. AKU's culture of love and appreciating staff has been a key motivator.
Tell us about your best moment at AKUHN

In 2004, I got promoted as the lead person at the filing section, a position that came with a huge responsibility as the hospital was expanding and the university was being established. As years progressed, I found myself fitting in the shoes of the supervisor, assistant manager to my current position of manager and advisor to records management at both the main campus and outreach centres.  I am currently heavily involved in the design and deployment of our future patient records management system, managing a team of 31 people.
Something significant that you have been part of?

Being part of the team that was responsible with the expansion of departmental tasks including establishment of the cancer registry, Transcription Service, and Electronic Document Management system (EDMS).
What are you most proud of working at AKU?
Transformation of current medical records to an information centre which made quality and accurate information available for the hospital.
You are an integral part of AKU's day-to-day operations - tell us about this impact

Supporting the Postgraduate Medical Education programme through facilitation of patient records for student research and ensuring safety and quick access to patient information during the continuity of care.
Any growth in your personal life?

I am blessed to have two children, the first born will be celebrating his 28th birthday this year. AKUHN also gave me an opportunity to further my education and I am a proud holder of a Bachelors of Arts in Leadership Management degree from St Paul's University (2010) and a Diploma in Records Management (2006). I intend to enroll for a Master's Degree in the near future.
Who has benefited from your leadership?

Some of the staff who worked under my supervision have been promoted to various capacities. Top of mind is Jeremiah Munene (HOD at Kenya Medical Training College)  Athony Muruga (AKUH Kisumu), Nathan Akorosi (Kenya Medical Research Institute) and Pauline Njuita (AKUHN outreach division).
What you would like to see implemented at AKU?
Implementation of an Electronic Health Records (EHR) system, where we can use data from patient records to improve quality outcomes through their care management programs.
Any plans to retire soon?
(Laughs) I am very much around. I am actually looking forward to you visiting our department.
